review_notes: Reviewed all 112 lines, the underlying Gram and mass definitions, both decrement lemmas, and downstream uses. One useful generalisation is supported directly by the existing envelope theorem. No replacement was executed or compilation-tested.

findings.problem: The statement identifies the number of harmonic coordinates with the Gaussian scaling exponent. The underlying envelope theorem already treats these independently, so this restriction prevents applying the dyadic equivalence formulation to smaller harmonic spans, such as a single coordinate on a higher-dimensional space.
findings.proposed_change:
In the existing section context, generalise the statement to:

theorem dyadicHeatGram_upper (m : ℕ)
    (hρ : 0 < ρ) (hρr : ρ < r) (hκ : 0 ≤ κ)
    {R A D η lambda : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) (hlambda : 0 < lambda)
    (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hD : 0 < D) (hη : 0 ≤ η)
    (hreg : 2 * κ * (L : ℝ) ^ 2 + η ≤ lambda) (i : ℕ)
    (herror : ∀ t ∈ Icc ((R / 2 ^ i) ^ 2 / 4) ((R / 2 ^ i) ^ 2),
      ‖harmonicHeatError μ hQ (k := ker) G χ t p‖ ≤ η)
    (hgaussian : ∀ t ∈ Icc ((R / 2 ^ i) ^ 2 / 4) ((R / 2 ^ i) ^ 2),
      ∀ q : ℝ, 0 ≤ q → ∀ z, q * (R / 2 ^ i) ≤ dist p z →
        (χ.weight : X → ℝ) z * ker t p z ≤
          (A / (R / 2 ^ i) ^ (m + 2)) * Real.exp (-q ^ 2 / D))
    (v : Euclidean n) :
    ⟪v, ((dyadicHeatGram μ hQ hk U χ hR hlambda i : Euclidean n →L[ℝ] Euclidean n) -
      (dyadicHeatGram μ hQ hk U χ hR hlambda (i + 1) : Euclidean n →L[ℝ] Euclidean n)) v⟫_ℝ ≤
      dyadicHeatEnvelopeConstant M m A D R lambda η *
        ⟪v, dyadicBochnerEnvelope M (m + 2) p R i v⟫_ℝ

Use the existing proof, passing hgaussian directly to gaussian_dyadic_heat_increment_envelope and finishing with exact hb after the existing time rewrite. This changes the scaling parameter independently of the coordinate dimension, rather than merely deleting a binder. Retain R > 0 and lambda > 0. The formulation permits n = 0 or n = 1; the zero-dimensional conclusion is trivial, and m = 0 still means scaling exponent 2. The original statement follows by rewriting with hn.
findings.benefit: Users can reuse the same dyadic upper bound for scalar or lower-dimensional harmonic families without padding coordinates or reproducing the time-reindexing proof.

def dyadicBochnerEnvelope (M : PositiveBilinearMeasure X E) (n : ℕ)
    (p : X) (R : ℝ) (i : ℕ) : E →L[ℝ] E :=
  (3 / 4 : ℝ) ^ i • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ E +
    ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (i + 1), (3 / 4 : ℝ) ^ (i - j) • dyadicBochnerMass M n p R j
